field_changes.before: Converts finite nonnegative millisecond numbers to fractional Duration values; PTY objects default to 80 by 24 and require dimensions representable as u16.
field_changes.after: Duration conversion uses Duration::from_millis when as_u64 succeeds; otherwise only finite, nonnegative as_f64 values proceed to Duration::from_secs_f64(ms / 1000.0), without an upper representable-range guard. PTY objects default to 80 by 24 and require dimensions representable as u16.

before: This adapter does not expose maxRssBytes or pipe backpressure at this source revision. hex_bytes consumes pairs and accepts a final single hex digit; schema.rs reuses the same parser rather than requiring even length.
after: This adapter does not expose maxRssBytes or pipe backpressure at this source revision. hex_bytes consumes pairs and accepts a final single hex digit; schema.rs reuses the same parser rather than requiring even length.

A sufficiently large finite nonnegative value on the floating-point duration branch can exceed Duration's representable range and reach the panicking Duration::from_secs_f64 conversion instead of returning this adapter's Err. schema.rs accepts numeric timeoutMs/graceMs options without that upper bound; this is a source/API boundary, not an observed panic.

field_changes.before: Only Fail::Product is eligible for pending treatment; malformed or missing expected fields are harness failures.
field_changes.after: Only Fail::Product is eligible for pending under the suite's other conditions. An absent ordinary field in the returned field map becomes Fail::Harness through string conversion, whereas an expected partial result absent from Error::result() explicitly yields Fail::Product. Malformed expectation shapes are checked during Scenario::load through Names::step and schema::step/schema::expect (including pieces/entries validation), with load errors classified as Harness; the comparator alone is not the complete shape validator.

limits: Documentary identity, exact field-diff and source-quote checks only; no semantic decision or runtime result is inferred.
